answers.note: Three well-mixed grids with an accurate, detailed answer key, but several questions (link and 'why' items) need extended answers and difficulty is not signalled with marks or points.

Strong 12-square interleaved grid with confidence ratings and a full key, but no marks weighting by age of material and the misconception note wrongly implies William of Normandy was not king in 1066 (he was crowned on 25 December 1066).
Covers all three periods with an accurate key, but it is a thin seven-row prompt table with open 'why did it matter' columns rather than specific short questions, and no variation in difficulty.
Comprehensive, accurate card set with precise terminology, explain-why cards and calculations, but guidance on spaced self-testing is only a one-line afterthought.
Clean, accurate one-idea cards with clear spaced-practice instructions, but the set is short and never uses 'frequency of collisions', with the surface area explanation left imprecise.
Accurate, interleaved one-idea cards using precise terms, with correct calculations and a concrete spaced-retrieval schedule over the eight weeks.
Fully worked five mornings with minute-by-minute recall tasks, kn/gn mixed in daily, a simple rule, transfer words and teacher tracking of who is still wrong.
Varied, timed sessions with the rule explained simply, but Thursday's silent letter hunt has children copy words and teacher tracking is only of class-wide common problems via self-checking.

Recall-based with a clear rule and a marked Friday dictation to see who needs reteaching, but the sessions are thin, with six-minute tasks that would not genuinely fill the time (e.g. a two-word rule hunt).
